[H1]I didn’t lose, I was strategically betrayed by my own dice![/H1] Thank you to the developers for the curator copy. This is nonetheless an impartial review. 2026 is shaping up nicely for hidden indie gems, and this one fits right into that category. It mixes tabletop roguelike vibes with dice-based scoring that will remind you of [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/2379780/Balatro/]Balatro[/url], wrapped in a darker, slightly unsettling atmosphere that wouldn’t feel out of place next to [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1092790/Inscryption/]Inscryption[/url]. Early runs feel forgiving, then the systems start stacking and the thinking ramps up. You have a surprising amount of control over your fate: dice types and materials, booster cards, permanent items, and even which events you’ll face (to a point). The whole thing becomes a constant push-and-pull between planning ahead and tempting fate, hoping to reach always higher scores. [B]PROS[/B] The mechanics are easy to grasp but hard to fully master and the visual presentation is nailing it: the menus are all pirate-themed, there's a stylish opening sequence, and the moody tone fits the ambiance perfectly. There’s a good variety of events and environments, a balanced difficulty curve overall (even if the Abyss has a personal vendetta against me), and a ridiculous amount of possible combinations to experiment with. I really liked how movement on the map becomes its own resource-management puzzle, letting you gamble with random advancement or spend limited tools to choose your path. Add well-designed achievements, a challenge mode unlocked later on, and a solid save system that drops you back into your last event if you quit mid-run, and you obtain a game I still don't know how many hours I'll sink into, but it'll definitely reach the 3-digits numbers. [B]CONS[/B] But it can still use some polish. Repetition can show up across multiple runs, with some events repeating exactly the same way, which is kind of inevitable for the genre but still noticeable. Story mode also isn’t as relaxed as it first appears, especially if you’re chasing specific achievements at the same time, and challenge mode is blocked behind it. A few quality-of-life tweaks would also help a lot, like selecting or deselecting all dice at once, or skipping dialogue during repeat runs. [B]TIPS & TRICKS[/B] A few things worth knowing before the dice betray you: sail buttons that move you a fixed number of spaces carry over between maps in the same run, so burning them early can come back to bite you later. Some dice can be saved for future runs, and that small advantage can really snowball. Not every stop on the map is optional, so don’t dump resources right before a forced event. Coins disappear quickly too, since rerolls, ship upgrades, and strong items spike in price rapidly, making short, efficient plays to grab a maximum of coins key to staying alive. Overall, between smart mechanics, the strong atmosphere, and that constant tempting pull to play just a bit more, this one has officially taken over my casual Balatro runs. Less eye strain, immaculate vibes, and always plenty more to uncover. [h3]This review won't do the game justice...[/h3] TL;DR - Buy it. The game is stunningly (and creepily) beautiful, "relaxed" yet very engaging and satisfying. You're fished out of the sea by pirates (naturally) and this mysterious game appears with you. You're rolling dice which are scored with different multiplies for each combo type (pair, 2 pair, 3 of a kind). There are also cards/deckbuilding, trinkets, and dice variants that all affect the rules. (For example, maybe you roll 4 of kind, but you have an active card giving you a higher multiplier if you only "play" 3 of a kind.) As the pirate ship moves around the game board, there are encounters/events, trades, merchants, mini-games. I know, I know ... sounds boring. But it's very "satisfying" to play. It doesn't feel "RNG" at all as you have control over what dice/cards are in play, a limited number of re-rolls, the ability to purchase different cards that play to your strengths, and even have limited control of movement on the game board (to force or avoid certain events). Love it. Game seemed to just drop out of nowhere with no fanfare ... it deserves more attention!

好！（此评论开篇虽然才一个字，但语法严谨，用词工整，结构巧妙，朗朗上口可谓言简意赅不多不少，足见评论人扎实的文字功底<蜜汁自信>，以及信手拈来的写作技巧和惨绝人寰的创造能力，令人由衷佩服，再加上以感叹号收尾，实在是点睛之笔<手动耍帅>） 确实好哈，不吹不黑，起码基本功方面是能给高分的，如按钮布局，音效配合，易用便捷，跟手响应等，能看出来作者的心意和付出；对于一个小厂来说，能呈现出这样的效果已经ok了，可以推荐。如果还在犹豫，可以看看更多评论和商店演示，是骡子是马再多多感受综合评估一下，到那时再决定是否入库吧。 玩法上，《黑帆赌局》是一款海盗主题的肉鸽骰子构建游戏。选牌，投骰，叠加增益，打造属于咱的离谱组合。虽然离谱，但别忘了，海上没有所谓道理，海上只讲拳头；所以要小心，有时候你靠火炮取胜，有时候也需要策略，还有时候要点非酋，当骰子点数战胜万难的时候成就之情无以言表。 美术表现也是给力的加分项，诡异的氛围刻画，海盗风格的体现，卡牌年代的质感，棋盘场景的塑造等；无论是主角手臂的动作，还是书页的翻开，亦或船长的演出，都是惟妙惟肖恰到好处，可以加强更深的沉浸体验，使人愿看爱看多看，乃至愿玩爱玩多玩。 后台需要自动静音。窗口模式的分辨率设置，选项的显示和实际大小不符。一些特有术语或关键词，需要有说明；比如基数我还以为是倍率，实际是分值。建议推出支持者dlc，方便粉丝或者大佬更多可能的支持。适合触屏操控，可推出移动版以带来更多可能收益。ps, xbox, switch等主机若可以也希望上架。

[h1] TL;DR - [b]Undisclosed use of generative AI[/b] in cutscenes. [/h1] I confess - I usually love these kinds of casual roguelites. So I was excited to see a new one drop, and get it on sale! So disappointed to see what looked like generative AI in the [i]literal opening cutscene.[/i] Still, I checked the Steam page and didn't see any AI disclaimers, so I tried to give the game a fair shot. I'm a hobbyist animator myself - I thought maybe the animators had used a lot of tweening to save on cost, and I was just jumping to conclusions. Eventually I get to the final tower, and another cutscene plays... [i]the dots on the dice can't even stay consistent.[/i] [b][u]It was so blatantly, undeniably AI.[/u][/b] I wish the use of AI was disclosed this on the Steam page, because I wouldn't have given this project my money if I'd known. Both cutscenes were so vague (duh, it's generative AI) that they failed to establish anything about the setting at all aside from "pirate theme with vague supernatural elements", which the game doesn't [i]need[/i] an opening cutscene to do! The whole point of cutscenes is to provide an insight into the world outside of the limitations of the game itself. I'm not asking for professionally animated cutscenes - that's expensive. But I'd rather nothing than literal pointless slop. Anyways. I feel stupid and I should've known. I was hoping this would give me a similar experience to Act 1 of [i]Inscryption,[/i] but that game had heart, artistry and love baked into its very core. I cannot say the same about [i]Pirate's Gambit.[/i] I'm going to go see if I can get my money back.

The game is really good, was a lot of fun actually. The only issue is, it's lacking when it comes to content. I finished an entire run along with the challenge tower in under 90min. The synergies aren't diverse enough to entice me to keep going for another run. A lot of cards are just flat ability modifiers that doesn't really give depth to the gameplay (+15X, +10Y, etc...). Even the special die aren't really that interesting, just more of what the cards do. Also, I wouldn't call the game difficult, you're very limited in what you can accomplish with 5 die and the mercy of RNG. Either the run works out, or it doesn't. Like Balatro, but without having 10 cards in hand, instead you have only 5. I wish I can give this game a maybe. It's not bad, especially that I don't care about the AI cutscenes which others have pointed out. (Yes it's obvious they used AI to animate their artwork, but I can tell the art itself wasn't generated through AI)

All the cutscenes are blatantly AI generated, which destroys any enjoyment that I could have had for this game for me. They don't even give any information, the lighthouse scene is just a minute long of a morphed image of waves and what is supposedly supposed to be the player character standing atop it, despite the the areas being completely different shapes, changing from a dome to a platform. I was really looking forward to this game's full release after playing the demo of what looked to be a really well built game; each card was viable in the right decks and combinations, and there was barely anything that was a straight upgrade from a different card. If the cutscenes were removed, or even swapped out for something that wasn't churned out by a lazy developer, (like the sounds that were up to interpretation in the demo) I would consider playing the game. One more thing, you don't really notice the ai in the first cutscene, but once you get to the second one (Just after 2 hours of gameplay, which coincidentally is the playtime cap for refunds) it's obvious. Do not buy this game.

我们的命运就像是这旋转的骰子一样，永远也无法未知下一步将会发生什么，会带来财富？还是毁灭？《黑帆赌局》这是一个考验勇气与智慧以及运气的游戏，游戏中融合了类似热门的《小丑牌》玩法，不同的骰子材质、得分骰型以及卡牌遗物等，再结合写实的画面表现，使得新鲜的体验感不断。并且游戏给喜欢挑战性的玩家在后续的关卡中增加不同的难题，使得玩家要在游玩的过程中随机应变，体验不同的打法流派的乐趣，值得一试。
Plundering excitement awaits in this strategic sea escapade. Just when you think you've got the loot in sight, the tide turns. A thrilling mix of chance and cunning.
Traverse uncharted lands, uncover the ship’s long-buried secrets. To survive, you must build your deck wisely, master the dice and items, and make each move count.
A great roguelike based on the Yatch dice game (ancestor of the Yahtzee) set in the pirate area. Every run should be different with plenty of cards, custom dice, events and curse to alter your run.
